approach: Fix the root cause where a reading is accepted: add one refusal check, `check_timing_claim(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, wired as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` (reading/checks.rs:520-551) right after `check_records_measure` (line 541). It uses the gate every sibling check uses, `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion` (surveys.rs:237). A reading is inside the gate only if it has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, and a behavior criterion. Within the gate, the trigger is lexical and per segment (a newline, `;` or `. ` ends a segment). It reads the request, the summary and every criterion that does not declare `newly refused`. A segment is a timing claim when it holds a speed or delay phrase (`speed up`, `faster`, `slower`, `too slow`, `shorten`, `quicker`, `delay`, `earlier`, `sooner`) and EITHER a duration figure (a number with a unit such as `12 minutes`, `90s`, `500ms`) OR, for the strong speed phrases only, a stage noun (`pipeline`, `test suite`, `tests`, `ci`, `checks`, `compile`, `build`, `stage`). Phrases are matched with `has_phrase`, with hyphen and underscore read as a space, so `delayer` and `speed-up` are handled. The reading must then carry a `Timeline:` assumption that holds all five parts: a `crates/` path (`names_crates_path`), at least two duration figures, a stage-order marker (`then`, `->`, `→`, `=>`, `before`, `after`), a source label (`measured`, `recorded`, `estimate` or `estimated`), and a word naming where the claim sits (`claimed`, `claim` or `delay`). The error names the matched phrase and where it was found, says the `Timeline:` assumption is missing or lists the parts missing from the nearest one, and gives an example that itself satisfies the check. Tests, a corpus case and a declared-share test follow the `check_records_measure` pattern. CHANGELOG.md and a new D190 name the root cause. No prompt file, config file or reader rule line changes.

decisions.choice: Gate the check with `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, read the request, summary and criteria, and exempt any reading with a criterion declaring `newly refused` readings.

rejected.option: Scan the reading only, not the request
rejected.why: The figure enters in the request. A reader that drops it from the summary would hide the claim from the check.

rejected.option: Apply to every reading with a capability
rejected.why: Docs readings and the fake reader's readings would be refused for words alone, which raises the refusal rate with no benefit.

rejected.option: Add a reader rule line to READING_RULES or edit a prompt file
rejected.why: The reader brief test pins `READING_RULES.len() == 14` (athena-context briefs.rs:4415) and the reader prompt has 2 tokens left. `check_history_fixture` has no rule line either. The refusal text reaches the reader on its second read (`read_for`).

decisions.choice: Trigger on a speed or delay phrase plus a duration figure, or a strong speed phrase plus a stage noun, within one segment. `earlier` and `delay` count only with a figure.
decisions.reason: The 8hzb shape (`move the call earlier ... about 12 minutes`) is caught by the figure branch. The c453 and eebk shape (`speed up the tests`, no figure) is caught by the stage-noun branch. `earlier` appears in ordinary phrases such as `earlier job` and `earlier attempt` (refusal_corpus.rs:267-274), so it never triggers alone. A grep of crates/**/*.rs found no existing fixture with a speed phrase beside a duration figure except comments and Hestia tests that never reach the gate (checks.rs:659, hestia.rs:6403, 6735).

rejected.why: `faster` and `earlier` occur in ordinary readings. The refusal rate would exceed the 10% replay hold.
The c453 and eebk jobs asked to speed up tests with no figure. Only the figure branch would miss two of the three jobs the request cites.

decisions.choice: Judge the Timeline by five lexical parts (a crates/ path, at least two duration figures, an order marker, a source label, a word naming where the claim sits), best assumption first, and name the missing parts in the error.
decisions.reason: This is the same structure as `check_records_measure`'s three-part test (surveys.rs:547-586). The three introspections each ask for the stage order, the measured duration per stage and the place of the claimed delay. A model-judged check would cost a call and fail the 'by mechanism' default. The limit is stated in the doc comment: the check proves the Timeline is there, not that its figures are true. The planner and the critic still judge that, and the verifier runs the criterion.

rejected.option: Accept any `Timeline:` assumption that names a crates/ path
rejected.why: That is `check_code_survey`'s weakness. An empty timeline with a path would pass.

rejected.option: Run the code or the records to measure the timeline inside the check
rejected.why: Out of scope and not possible: the check reads the reading only, with no repository or records, as its siblings do.

decisions.choice: Signature `check_timing_claim(reading: &Reading, request: &str)`, called as `step!(check_timing_claim(reading, request));` between `check_records_measure` and `check_design_existing_code`.
decisions.reason: `check_governance_coverage(reading, request)` (checks.rs:543) already shows the form. Every `step!` line has a corpus case (refusal_corpus.rs:2905). No test pins the successor of `check_records_measure`: the existing order tests at reading.rs:8234 and 8714 pin only the predecessor of `check_history_fixture` and `check_records_measure`. A grep for `check_design_existing_code(reading)` finds only checks.rs:542.

decisions.choice:
Input forms the rule handles, each mapped to a corpus case. New cases are added in `timing_claim_cases()`, and their tags are added to `INPUT_FORMS` (63 becomes the new length).
- Dash bullet with a speed claim and a figure, no Timeline: existing tag `dash-bullet`, new case `timing-claim-figure-no-timeline-8hzb`, Refuse(check_timing_claim).

- Timeline with a path but no durations or order: new tag `timeline-missing-parts`, case `timing-claim-timeline-without-durations`, Refuse.

decisions.choice:
Exits of the new stage `check_timing_claim` (a pure function of `reading` and `request`):
- Success, no claim (not gated, or no trigger, or a `newly refused` declaration): returns Ok; `step!` falls through (checks.rs:528-533) to `check_design_existing_code`. No state is left.
- Success, claim with a satisfying Timeline: returns Ok; same path.
- Fail, claim without a satisfying Timeline: returns Err; `step!` returns `Some(("check_timing_claim", error))`. `read_once` (reading.rs:732-741) turns it into `Err((rule, text))`; reading.rs:750-764 stores a `ReadingAttempt` with the refusal (text redacted) and the reader reads a second time with the refusal as its correction. `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:499-502) returns the error to the other callers (plan, drain, steward `queued_work`, `check_reading_text` at replay.rs:54-64).
- Error (I/O): cannot happen; no file, git, network or record is read.
- Hold and interrupt: cannot happen; synchronous, no waiting or kill-switch read.
The per-rule refusal count in status takes the name from `stringify!`, so no list needs an entry.

risks.risk: The lexical trigger refuses readings it should not, such as a stage noun beside `faster` in an unrelated sentence.
risks.mitigation: Both triggers need a speed phrase and are limited to code or tests readings with a behavior criterion. `earlier` and `delay` need a figure. A refusal-rule reading that declares `newly refused` is exempt. The producer runs `cargo test --locked`. A repo grep found no fixture with a speed phrase beside a figure that reaches the gate. The share is declared at 4%, and the replay at verification measures it against the 10% hold.

risks.risk: A Timeline can satisfy the lexical parts with invented figures, and a claim stated without a figure or stage noun is missed.
risks.mitigation: This is stated in the doc comment's `Limits:`. A request that gives its figure as words (`a minute`) triggers only through the stage-noun branch. The planner's and critic's existing prose rules, and the verifier running the criteria, remain the guard for the truth of the timeline.

risks.risk: The gate short-circuits, so the 8hzb-style test request may be refused first by another check such as `check_outcome_state` (for delivery words) or `check_defined_terms` (for structural terms).
risks.mitigation: The producer picks request wording for the gate-level tests that no earlier check refuses, and asserts the refusing check by name, as `refuser_for` tests already do (reading.rs:7300). The direct `check_timing_claim` call needs no such care.

risks.risk: This job's own reading, replayed later from stored records, would count as newly refused if it carried no declaration.
risks.mitigation: The root-cause reading already carries no Timeline. The criterion 5 text and the doc declare the 4% share, and the exemption for a declared `newly refused` reading covers a refusal-rule reading. The replay excludes the running job (replay.rs:142-146).

demonstrations.method:
Tests in the reading.rs test module, next to the records-measure tests.
1. Build the 8hzb-style reading with `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])` and set the summary and request to a sentence such as `Move the status call earlier in the run to save about 12 minutes`. Call `refuser_for(&reading, request)`, and assert `Some("check_timing_claim")`, the error text and `check_timing_claim` directly. The producer must pick request words that no earlier check refuses (the gate short-circuits).
2. Push a `Timeline:` assumption that names `crates/athena-core/src/run.rs`, the stages in order with figures (`reading 2 min (recorded) then planning 6 min (recorded) then verification 5 min (estimate)`) and `the claimed 12 minute delay sits in verification`. Assert `refuser_for` is None.
3. Parts removed one at a time (no path, one figure, no order marker, no label, no claim word) each refuse and name the missing part.
4. The example in the error text, extracted as in reading.rs:8543-8547, satisfies the check when pushed as an assumption.
5. A reading with no speed or delay claim, and one whose only criterion declares `expected 4% of newly refused readings`, are not refused by this check.
6. Spellings: `speed-up`, `Speed Up`, `90s`, `500ms` trigger; `delayer` does not.
7. `check_reading_text(&reading, request)` refuses and then accepts with the same texts, the stored-reading seam used by drain, plan and `athena check-reading`.
demonstrations.observes: The 8hzb-style reading with a claim and no Timeline is refused by `check_timing_claim` with an error naming `Timeline:`. It is accepted once a Timeline holds the path, order, durations, label and claim word. An ordinary reading is untouched.

The no-claim test (an ordinary reading, no speed or delay phrase) passes in both cases, so the check is not a blanket refusal.
